recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Andrew Crowley**, 46, was sentenced to a two-year suspended sentence for attempting to defraud **Sotheby’s** by selling fake ancient statues.  Crowley presented forged invoices claiming the statues were from 1976 and used printing methods that were 25 years too modern. Forensic analysis revealed the documents were fabricated, and the judge acknowledged Crowley did not intend to deceive but instead believed he inherited the items legitimately. **Sotheby’s** experts identified inconsistencies in the paperwork early on, preventing a potential fraud.

recent_articles.title: Gas explosion at Chinese coal mine kills at least 90 | Mining News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A gas explosion at a coal mine in Qinyuan county, Shanxi province, has killed at least 90 people. The blast occurred at the Liushenyu mine, where 247 workers were on duty when the explosion ripped through the facility.  **President Xi Jinping** called for intensified efforts to prevent major accidents following the incident. Rescue operations are ongoing as emergency crews search for survivors. **Xinhua**, the state-run broadcaster, reported that the person responsible for overseeing the mine has been arrested while authorities investigate the cause of the explosion.

recent_articles.title: US jury finds Boeing not guilty in 737 MAX grounding lawsuit - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A US jury ruled in favor of **Boeing**, finding the aerospace giant not liable for lost revenue claims from Polish airline LOT. LOT had accused **Boeing** of fraud and sought $250 million in compensation for alleged false representations concerning its 737 MAX jets, which were grounded for 20 months following two deadly crashes.  The jury's decision comes after a series of lawsuits related to the MAX crashes, including settlements with victim families and a criminal charge dismissal against **Boeing** as part of an agreement with US prosecutors.

recent_articles.title: Race for French presidency sees ex-PM Philippe as early favourite to beat populists
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Edouard Philippe**, the former prime minister of **Emmanuel Macron**, is emerging as the frontrunner in the French presidential race.  He is seen as the only candidate capable of defeating a hard-right candidate, such as **Marine Le Pen**, or her deputy **Jordan Bardella**.  Philippe's campaign strategy focuses on appealing to center-right voters and positioning himself as a barrier against far-right populism. However, challenges remain, including potential rivalries within the center-right, the ongoing corruption probe into Philippe, and the unpredictable nature of the political landscape. The outcome of the race will likely hinge on the performance of **Marine Le Pen** and her party, the National Rally (RN), as well as the strength of the hard-left candidate, **Jean-Luc Mélenchon**.

recent_articles.title: Innovation begins with understanding the fundamentals: Prakash Balasubramanian - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prakash Balasubramanian**, senior director at **Infineon Technologies**, emphasized the importance of foundational knowledge for technological breakthroughs during the inauguration of "Nirmaan Utsav" in Kalaburagi city. Deputy Commissioner of Police (Law and Order) Shaloo encouraged students to combine academic learning with practical experience and stay updated on emerging fields like drones, artificial intelligence, and cybersecurity. HKE Society president and MLC Shashil Namoshi noted that **PDA Engineering College** is nurturing future-ready students through events like "Nirmaan Utsav."

recent_articles.title: US says temporary visa holders should leave to apply for Green Cards | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS)** issued new guidance stating that obtaining a Green Card within the US is discretionary, not automatic. The Department of Homeland Security said this policy aims to ensure immigration procedures are followed rather than allowing individuals to remain in the US while seeking permanent residency through "loopholes."  Rights groups criticized the move, warning it could force vulnerable migrants to return to unsafe conditions while awaiting decisions on their applications.

recent_articles.title: Slovenia’s parliament approves right-wing Janez Jansa as prime minister | Government News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Slovenia’s parliament** voted to approve **Janez Jansa**, a right-wing populist, as prime minister.  Jansa's appointment follows a post-election stalemate and marks a shift from the country's previous liberal government. The new coalition government, formed by **Jansa’s Slovenian Democratic Party (SDS)** and several center-right groups, will hold 43 seats in the assembly. Jansa has previously served as prime minister from 2004 to 2008, 2012 to 2013, and 2020 to 2022.  He plans to prioritize economic growth, fighting corruption, and decentralization.

recent_articles.title: Power Division warns consumers against fake subsidy links, QR code scams - Business - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Ministry of Energy’s Power Division** issued a warning to consumers about fraudulent activities targeting electricity bill subsidies. The **Power Division** advised against clicking on suspicious links or QR codes, as criminals are attempting to steal personal information through these methods.  Consumers were urged not to share any personal details for obtaining subsidies and law enforcement agencies have been informed of the scam.

recent_articles.title: NCCIA uncovers gang selling data of govt officials to foreign entities; four arrested - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA)** arrested four individuals in South Punjab for selling sensitive personal data of government officers to foreign entities. The suspects, identified as Arshad Tariq, Arham Bari, Anam Sabir and Mohammad Rizwan, were allegedly sharing the data with foreign intelligence agencies.  **The NCCIA** is investigating how the information was accessed and has directed government institutions to strengthen data security.

recent_articles.title: Bolivia in crisis: Social unrest, demands for president to resign escalate | Protests News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rodrigo Paz**, Bolivia's president, is facing growing social unrest and demands for his resignation.  The protests began over a convergence of sector-based demands, including wage increases, contaminated fuel issues, and land classification changes. **Indigenous groups** from the highlands escalated the protests by blocking roads, demanding the president step down. Former President **Evo Morales**, who was ousted in 2019, has mobilized his supporters to pressure **President Paz**. The government is attempting to address legitimate demands while also cracking down on those deemed hostile to democracy.  The unrest has led to violence and clashes between protesters and police, with over 120 people detained.  **Jose Luis Lupo**, the Presidency Minister, stated that the government will use dialogue for legitimate sectors and full force of the law against those attacking democracy. The situation remains fluid as authorities seek a path forward.

recent_articles.title: Why is the US putting pressure on Cuba and what are Trump's aims?
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The United States is escalating pressure on Cuba, accusing the country of posing a national security threat and recently indicting former leader Raúl Castro. The US has imposed an oil blockade, sanctions, and a murder indictment against Castro, citing an incident in 1996 where Cuban fighter jets shot down two civilian planes owned by Cuban exiles.  Cuba maintains its actions were justified as self-defense within its airspace and accuses the US of using the charges to justify military aggression. The US has also targeted senior Cuban officials accused of human rights abuses or corruption, while offering $100 million in aid through humanitarian organizations. Cuba's response has been characterized by fiery rhetoric, with leaders demanding an end to the blockade and accusing the US of "coercion" and threats. China and Russia have condemned the US pressure on Cuba.

recent_articles.title: ACB books Medchal deputy collector in disproportionate assets case - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB)** officials conducted searches on **Marri Vamshi Mohan**, a Special Grade Deputy Collector, and his associates following allegations of acquiring assets beyond known sources of income. The searches uncovered properties valued at around ₹6.22 crore, including land plots, houses, and vehicles, along with cash and gold ornaments. **Vamshi Mohan** was arrested and remanded to judicial custody.  The investigation is ongoing.

recent_articles.title: Turkiye shutters liberal Istanbul university seized in criminal probe | Education News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **President Recep Tayyip Erdogan** revoked the operating license for Istanbul Bilgi University, a private university known for its liberal values, citing insufficient education standards. The closure, effective immediately, follows a criminal investigation into the institution's parent company and has sparked protests from students who will now continue their studies at Mimar Sinan University. **The Council of Higher Education** promised to ensure student safety during this transition.

recent_articles.title: Marco Rubio visits India: What’s at stake with Trump-Modi ties strained? | International Trade News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Marco Rubio**, US Secretary of State, is visiting India for a three-day trip ahead of the Quad meeting on May 26th. The visit also coincides with the US Department of Justice dropping criminal fraud charges against Indian billionaire **Gautam Adani**, and an extension of a sanctions waiver allowing purchases of Russian oil.  Rubio's trip is seen as part of Washington's effort to strengthen bilateral relations with India, particularly in light of tensions between Trump and Modi last year.

recent_articles.title: Indian man sentenced to 15.5 years in prison for gold scam in US, picked 16 gold bars from elderly victims - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Syed M Makki**, a 38-year-old Indian man, was sentenced to 15.5 years in prison for his role in a gold scam targeting elderly victims across the US.  The scheme involved malware that tricked victims into believing they were dealing with legitimate authorities, leading them to liquidate their savings and purchase gold bullion. **Makki** acted as a courier, collecting gold bars from victims and delivering them to co-conspirators. The Justice Department reported that the scam resulted in over $4.75 million in losses for victims.

recent_articles.title: Turkish opposition fights court ousting of leaders in ruling boosting Erdogan
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Turkish** opposition, led by Özgür Özel of the Republican People's Party (CHP), is challenging a court ruling removing them from leadership positions.
